findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/validate-command-timeout-smoke.ts:119,158,177 — new sections 6/7/8 create 3 fresh temp project roots via mkdtempSync(...) (each holding a written lattice.config.json) but never clean them up (no rmSync import/call anywhere in the file), unlike ~95% of comparable smoke tasks in packages/main/src/tasks/ (213/223 files using mkdtempSync also call rmSync, e.g. audit-esm-smoke.ts:7,37 which does `rmSync(root, { recursive: true, force: true })`). Because this file is registered in lattice.config.json validate.commands (line 59, focus: fast) and therefore runs on every `lattice validate` invocation going forward, this leaks 3 stray tmpdir directories per run indefinitely — a real, compounding resource-hygiene regression, not a one-off test artifact.

CHK-001:happy:2, CHK-001:edge:2, CHK-001:adversarial:2 (checklist.json) each assert RED/pre-fix ("current main") behavior of validate-command-timeout-smoke.js — exits 1, prints a FAIL line, section 6 fails while sections 1-5 pass. Every one of the 33 bound verificationEvidence entries (all 3 checklist items) carries the IDENTICAL receipt outputDigest 2846ab033bfe46f8813e65938364d2401a95447562c120b1ab694112d88dc37a / outputTail "validate-command-timeout smoke passed: 27 assertions\n" / exitCode 0 — i.e. a GREEN, post-fix run with no FAIL line. A passing-receipt cannot support a failing-state claim: these three intents have zero evidence that the RED state (documented only as a manual stash/rebuild/restore control experiment in plan.md CHK-001 Verify section) was ever captured. Even the checklist items own pinned verification.command/selector for these three intents is the same PASS-selector ("...passed: 27 assertions") smoke invocation, so no red-state proof was ever recorded, only re-confirmations of the current green state.

CHK-002 edge intents E-001 ("Bare-string config entries ... do not inject a spurious timeout"), E-003 ("Shell-style config entries (shell:true) cannot false-positive-match"), E-004 ("Config entry with timeoutMs:0 or negative value" on the NEW pinned-command path), and adversarial A-003/A-004, have NO corresponding check() assertion anywhere in packages/main/src/tasks/validate-command-timeout-smoke.ts. Grep confirms every validate.commands[] entry ever constructed in the file (lines 126,164,183-184) is object-form {command,args,timeoutMs} with a positive timeoutMs — no bare-string entry, no shell:true entry, and no timeoutMs:0/negative entry is ever written or fed through resolvePinnedCommandTimeoutMs. These 5 intents are pure code-reading/analytical claims about configuredValidationCommands/commandFromString/resolveCommandTimeoutMs behavior, yet are stamped kind:logic_test, mechanical:true, result:pass, bound to the same shared smoke-run receipt that passes for reasons entirely unrelated to these claims (the 27 assertions that do exist never touch bare-string, shell:true, or zero/negative-timeoutMs config entries).

CHK-002:H-002 ("Diff of checklist.ts shows exactly 4 call sites ... changed ... No duplicated matching logic exists outside the one helper"), CHK-002:H-003 ("git diff HEAD -- packages/main/src/core/validation-executor.ts packages/main/src/handlers/verifier.ts produces empty output"), CHK-002:E-005 ("tsc build succeeds ... Import graph is one-way"), and CHK-001:happy:0 ("npm --prefix packages/main run build exits 0") are all bound (per their own verificationIntent.verification.command field in checklist.json) to node packages/main/dist/tasks/validate-command-timeout-smoke.js, NOT to git diff or npm run build. Running the smoke script never invokes git diff or npm run build, so it is circumstantial at best (it would not run if the build were broken) but does not mechanically verify "git diff produces empty output" for the two named files, nor "exactly 4 call sites changed" in checklist.ts, nor does it re-execute npm run build at evidence-capture time. This is the coarse-grained-sharing failure mode the story description explicitly asked to be scrutinized: the shared command is not, for these 4 intents, actually the operation the claim requires.

CHK-001:happy:1 verificationIntent text (checklist.json) still describes plan.md CHK-001 original, pre-CORRECTION single-assertion design: "calls runSingleAllowlistedCommand with the matching command STRING and no options.timeoutMs, and asserts result.timedOut === true and result.code === 124." plan.md line 12-22 explicitly states that design "can NEVER turn green after CHK-002" and documents the CORRECTED split into 6a (validate-command-timeout-smoke.ts:137-138: direct call, no options.timeoutMs, asserts timedOut===false — a permanent characterization, NOT the red->green case) and 6b (lines 147-152: calls resolvePinnedCommandTimeoutMs then runSingleAllowlistedCommand WITH an explicit {timeoutMs: resolved} option, asserting timedOut===true/code===124). No single call in the implemented file matches happy:1 literal wording (no-options.timeoutMs AND timedOut===true together) — 6a has no-timeoutMs+false, 6b has explicit-timeoutMs+true. The checklist intent text was never updated to reflect the plan CORRECTION even though verificationEvidence for CHK-001:happy:1 is stamped result:pass.

packages/main/src/tasks/validate-command-timeout-smoke.ts:329-340 — section 12 (H-003 check) wraps BOTH the execSync(git diff) call AND the subsequent check(...) assertion inside the same try block, whose catch (line 338-339) only console.warns SOFT-SKIP and swallows the error rather than exiting 1. Since check() throws an Error on assertion failure (line 66: `if (!cond) throw new Error(...)`), a non-empty diffOutput (i.e. validation-executor.ts or verifier.ts actually WAS modified from main) throws inside the try and is caught by the same catch meant only for execSync/environment failures (e.g. unresolvable main ref) — so the assertion can NEVER cause a hard failure, it only ever prints a warning to stderr and the smoke keeps going / exits 0. Live repro: appended a trailing comment to validation-executor.ts, rebuilt, reran the smoke — output was `SOFT-SKIP git-diff-vs-main check (H-003) — FAIL: validation-executor.ts and verifier.ts are byte-for-byte unmodified from main (empty git diff)` followed by `validate-command-timeout smoke passed: 39 assertions` and exit code 0 (not 1). This is the exact scenario the check exists to catch (H-003: "validation-executor.ts and verifier.ts remain byte-for-byte unmodified"), and it is completely vacuous — this permanently-registered validate.commands entry (lattice.config.json:59) provides zero actual protection for the H-003 claim despite being cited as evidence for CHK-002:H-003.

packages/main/src/tasks/validate-command-timeout-smoke.ts:351-357 — section 13 (H-002 call-site count) asserts "exactly 4 call sites" by counting literal source-text occurrences of the substring `resolvePinnedCommandTimeoutMs(root, command)` in checklist.ts, rather than any semantic/AST-based check. This smoke is permanently registered in lattice.config.json:59 validate.commands, so it runs on every future `lattice validate`. Any purely cosmetic future change to checklist.ts that does not alter behavior at all — e.g. renaming either lambda parameter (command/cwd -> cmd/dir) at one call site, reformatting via a wider line-wrap that inserts a line break inside the argument list, or wrapping runCommand construction in a small local helper — would silently drop the matched count below 4 (or, in the case a future comment happens to mention the exact same literal substring, could mask a real missing-call-site regression by coincidentally keeping the count at 4). Either way this section validates the literal text shape of unrelated call sites rather than the actual behavior (that all 4 runSingleAllowlistedCommand invocations route their timeoutMs through the shared resolver), making it a maintenance trap: it can fail `lattice validate` for a no-op refactor with a cryptic message unrelated to any real regression, or silently pass despite a real duplication regression if the comment/text happens to coincide.

4 of the 32 deferred_gate_evidence waiver notes claim specific validate-command-timeout-smoke.ts sections "genuinely cover" an intent, but tracing the actual code shows they do not test the described scenario (underlying implementation is correct on manual probe -- this is a coverage-attribution error in the notes, not a functional bug). (1) CHK-002:E-001 note claims section 9 (smoke:226-251) covers "bare-string config entries never carry timeoutMs", but the chosen bareStringCommand = node -e "process.exit(0)" (smoke:234) contains parentheses matching verifier.ts SHELL_META_RE (/[;&|<>$()`]/, verifier.ts:72), so commandFromString (verifier.ts:151-160) takes the early shell:true/{args:[]} return, NOT the splitShellWords tokenization path E-001 is about. Verified empirically: configuredValidationCommands() on this exact input returns {command:"node -e \"process.exit(0)\"",args:[],shell:true} -- the same code path as section 10 (E-003), not a genuine bare-string match. (2) CHK-002:E-002 note claims sections 6a/6b (smoke:141-179) exercise "parsing parity between tokenizeCommandString and splitShellWords", but splitShellWords is never invoked anywhere in this file (grep confirms zero call sites) -- every config entry in the file is either object-form (bypasses splitShellWords entirely, e.g. sections 6-8/11/14) or the metachar-triggering bareStringCommand above. (3) CHK-002:A-001 note claims the same sections cover whitespace/quoting-evasion resistance; no test anywhere varies quoting/whitespace of a command between its config entry and its matching pinned string. (4) CHK-003:edge:1 note claims section 8 (smoke:201-224) covers the args-length/strict-prefix guard, but section 8s two config entries and two pinned commands all have EQUAL-length args differing only in content (that is edge:2s scenario, correctly covered) -- no length-mismatch/prefix case exists in the file. I manually verified via ad hoc probes against the compiled dist/handlers/checklist.js+verifier.js that the real resolvePinnedCommandTimeoutMs/configuredValidationCommands correctly handle all four scenarios (true bare strings tokenize+match correctly, whitespace variants normalize identically, prefix-length mismatches return undefined) -- so the fix itself is not defective, but these 4 waiver notes should either be corrected to admit the gap (not claim section coverage that is not there) or the smoke file should gain a genuinely non-shell-metacharacter bare string (e.g. node --version) plus a strict-prefix-args case, since this story is specifically about evidence integrity and the notes currently overstate what is tested.

checklist.json:130,140,150,493,534 (verificationEvidence waiver notes for CHK-001:happy:0, CHK-001:happy:1, CHK-001:happy:2, CHK-002:E-005, CHK-002:A-004) are each truncated at exactly 899-900 characters, cutting off mid-word/mid-sentence with no terminating punctuation (e.g. happy:1 ends "...replaced by the actually-implemented 6a/6b split (commit 63ec"; A-004 ends "...both the new resolv"). All 27 other waiver notes on this story end with a complete sentence and are well under 900 chars (518-876), confirming this is a hard ~900-char cap the DEV agent hit for these 5 rather than an intentional stop. The substantive claim in each is independently verifiable as true (confirmed by direct code/build/red-evidence inspection), so this is not a functional defect, but a waiver note that cuts off before finishing its own citation/justification is an incomplete explanation under review rule 2 ("waiver must have a clear note explaining why"), which is squarely this story's own theme (accurate evidence-completeness claims, per the F-008 finding this round already addressed for 4 other intentRefs). Fix: shorten/tighten these 5 notes so they conclude with a complete sentence within the same budget.
